decision_table.name: Determine_VT_Filing_Requirement
decision_table.description: Determine if corporation must file Vermont state corporate tax return. Checks for physical presence or economic nexus based on "doing business" standard.

condition.name: has_physical_presence
condition.comment: Has physical presence in VT (office, employees, property)

condition.name: has_economic_nexus
condition.comment: Meets VT economic nexus threshold or "doing business" standard

actions.action: // Physical nexus established - filing required // Apportionment will be calculated by tables 7000-7500

rule.policy:
VT filing required due to physical presence (office, employees, or property in state).
A corporation has physical presence nexus in VT if it has: - An office, store, warehouse, or other place of business in VT - Employees working in VT - Tangible personal property located in VT - Real property located in VT
Reference: 32 V.S.A. § 5833 (Nexus and apportionment) Reference: Vermont Department of Taxes Nexus Guidance

VT filing required due to economic nexus ("doing business" in Vermont).
Vermont applies a facts-and-circumstances "doing business" test for income tax nexus. Unlike sales tax (which uses $100,000 threshold), corporate income tax nexus is established when a corporation regularly solicits sales, provides services, or maintains ongoing customer relationships in Vermont, even without physical presence.
Economic activity creating nexus includes: - Systematic and regular business solicitation in VT - Maintaining customer relationships in VT - Providing services to VT customers - Deriving income from VT sources
Reference: South Dakota v. Wayfair, Inc., 138 S. Ct. 2080 (2018) Reference: Vermont Department of Taxes Economic Nexus Guidance Reference: 32 V.S.A. § 5833 (Doing business in Vermont)

No VT nexus - no filing requirement.
Corporation does not meet physical presence or "doing business" standards. Any estimated payments would be refunded.
Reference: 32 V.S.A. § 5833 (Nexus requirements)

decision_table.name: Calculate_VT_Income_Adjustments
decision_table.description: Calculate VT state-specific additions and subtractions to federal taxable income.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to calculate adjustments

rule.policy:
VT state-specific income adjustments to federal taxable income.
VT ADDITIONS to federal taxable income include: - Interest income from U.S. government obligations (exempt federally, taxable to VT) - Interest income from non-Vermont state and local bonds - State income taxes deducted on federal return - Certain federal/state depreciation differences - Expenses related to exempt income
VT SUBTRACTIONS from federal taxable income include: - Interest on Vermont state and municipal bonds - Vermont net operating loss deduction (subject to VT limitations) - Dividend income eligible for Vermont dividend received deduction - Certain refunds of state income taxes
Reference: Vermont Form BI-471 Instructions (Additions and Subtractions) Reference: 32 V.S.A. § 5832 (Adjustments to federal taxable income) Reference: Vermont Department of Taxes Corporate Tax Guidance

No nexus - no state adjustments calculated.
Corporation does not have VT nexus, so no income adjustments are needed.

decision_table.name: Calculate_VT_State_Tax
decision_table.description: Calculate VT state corporate income tax. Applies VT graduated tax rates (6.0%, 7.0%, 8.5%) to apportioned and adjusted taxable income. VT has one of the highest top corporate tax rates in the nation at 8.5%.

condition.name: has_nexus
condition.comment: Must have nexus to owe tax

rule.policy:
VT state corporate income tax calculation using graduated brackets:
1. Federal taxable income: [Form 1120 line 28] 2. Apportioned to VT: × [VT apportionment percentage] 3. VT additions: + [Federal interest, other state bond interest, etc.] 4. VT subtractions: - [VT municipal interest, VT NOL, etc.] 5. VT taxable income: = [Result] 6. VT tax calculation (graduated): - First $10,000: × 6.0% = $600 maximum - Next $15,000 ($10,001-$25,000): × 7.0% = $1,050 maximum - Over $25,000: × 8.5% 7. VT income tax: = [Tax before credits] 8. VT credits: - [R&D, affordable housing, renewable energy, historic preservation, etc.] 9. VT tax liability: = [Final tax]
VT uses single-sales factor apportionment (100% sales factor).
VT graduated tax structure (32 V.S.A. § 5832): - Tier 1: 6.0% on income $0-$10,000 - Tier 2: 7.0% on income $10,001-$25,000 - Tier 3: 8.5% on income over $25,000
The 8.5% top rate is one of the highest state corporate income tax rates in the nation, making Vermont a relatively high-tax state for corporations.
VT provides various tax credits including: - Research and development tax credit - Affordable housing tax credit - Renewable energy investment tax credit - Historic preservation tax credit - Economic advancement tax incentive
Reference: Vermont Form BI-471 (Business Income Tax Return) Reference: 32 V.S.A. § 5832 (Tax rates: 6.0%, 7.0%, 8.5%) Reference: 32 V.S.A. § 5833 (Single-sales apportionment) Reference: Vermont Department of Taxes Corporate Tax Bulletin 2025

No VT nexus - no tax liability.
Corporation does not have physical presence or economic nexus in VT. Any estimated payments are refunded.
Reference: 32 V.S.A. § 5833 (Nexus requirements)

No VT taxable income - no tax liability.
Corporation has VT nexus but no positive taxable income after apportionment and adjustments. Any estimated payments are refunded.
VT net operating loss (NOL) rules may apply: - VT allows NOL carryforward (conforming to federal rules as modified) - NOL deductions are subject to Vermont-specific limitations - VT may differ from federal NOL treatment for certain items
Reference: Vermont Form BI-471 (Business Income Tax Return) Reference: 32 V.S.A. § 5832 (Net operating loss deduction) Reference: Vermont Department of Taxes NOL Guidance
